For any vertex $v$, the ball of radius 3 around $v$ must be a tree to avoid cycles of length less than 7. If $v$ has degree 3, this tree contains at least $1 + 3 + 3(2) + 3(2)^2 = 22$ vertices. If $v$ has degree 4 or more, the tree contains at least $1 + 4 + 4(2) + 4(2)^2 = 29$ vertices. Since the graph has only 23 vertices, no vertex can have degree 4 or more, so the graph must be 3-regular (cubic). However, a cubic graph must have an even number of vertices (by the Handshaking Lemma), and 23 is odd. Thus, no such graph exists.
